title: Agent check on a 15-file dossier: the pharmacovigilance summary
about: The summary and the named qualified person are in a 4-page file among 15. Met in 20 model calls or fewer, and 150 000 input tokens or fewer.

Patient information leaflet

Corvane 500 mg film-coated tablets
Read all of this leaflet carefully before you start taking this medicine.
What Corvane is and what it is used for: Corvane lowers high blood pressure in adults.

Before you take Corvane

Do not take Corvane if you are allergic to corvanidine or any other ingredient of this medicine. Tell your doctor about all other medicines you take.

How to take Corvane

Always take this medicine exactly as your doctor has told you. The usual adult dose is one tablet (500 mg) twice daily with food. Do not exceed the prescribed dose.

How to store Corvane

Keep out of the sight and reach of children. Store below 30 °C in the original package. Do not use after the expiry date on the carton.

clauses.text: Summary of the system. The application shall include a summary of the applicant's pharmacovigilance system. The summary shall state where the pharmacovigilance master file is kept.
clauses.section_path: 4 Applications > Pharmacovigilance system summary > 4.1 Summary of the system

clauses.text: Qualified person. The summary shall name the qualified person responsible for pharmacovigilance and give that person's telephone number and email address.
clauses.section_path: 4 Applications > Pharmacovigilance system summary > 4.2 Qualified person

clauses.text: General provisions. The provisions of this guideline apply to every application submitted to the Authority after the date on which it takes effect. An application already under review when the guideline takes effect continues under the rules that applied when it was submitted, unless the applicant asks in writing to be assessed under this guideline. The Authority may issue notes that explain how a provision is applied. A note does not change a provision, and where a note and a provision differ, the provision applies. The applicant remains responsible for the accuracy of every statement in the application.

Format of documents. Documents shall be submitted in a searchable electronic format. Each document shall carry a title, a version number and a date, and shall show the name of the applicant and the product. Pages shall be numbered in sequence within a document. Where a document is a translation, the translation shall say so and shall name the language of the original. A document that cannot be read, or whose pages are out of order, may be returned to the applicant with a request to submit it again.

Declarations. The application shall include a declaration signed by a person authorised to act for the applicant. The declaration shall confirm that the information in the application is complete and correct, and that the samples supplied are representative of the product described. The Authority may ask for the declaration to be notarised. A false declaration is a ground for refusing or withdrawing a registration, without prejudice to any other measure the law provides.

Supporting information. The applicant may include supporting information that explains a choice made in the application, such as a literature review or a comparison with a reference product. Supporting information is considered with the rest of the application, but it does not replace a requirement of this guideline. Where supporting information is given in a language other than Arabic or English, a translation shall be provided.

Requests for information. Where the Authority needs more information to assess an application, it shall send the applicant a written request that states what is needed and the period for the reply. The applicant shall answer within that period. An answer shall be complete and shall refer to the request it replies to. If the applicant does not reply in time, the Authority may decide on the information it has or may close the application.

Changes during review. The applicant shall tell the Authority without delay of any change that affects the application while it is under review, such as a new manufacturing site, a change in the name or address of the applicant, or new data that bear on the safety or quality of the product. The Authority may ask for the documents to be updated. A change made without notice may be treated as a failure to provide complete information.

Confidentiality. Information supplied in an application is treated as confidential, except where the law requires it to be published. The applicant may mark a part of a document as commercially confidential and shall give the reason. The Authority decides whether the mark is justified, and shall tell the applicant before it publishes any part that was marked. Staff of the Authority are bound by a duty not to disclose confidential information.

Transitional provisions. A product registered before this guideline takes effect need not be re-submitted to meet its requirements. The first renewal of such a registration after the guideline takes effect shall comply with it. The Authority may set a later date for a particular requirement where compliance needs a long preparation, and shall publish the date and the reason.

law.title: Example Guideline on Stability Data for Registration

clauses.text: Scope. This guideline applies to applications to register a finished pharmaceutical product that will be stored and sold in climatic zone IVb, a hot and humid zone.
Long-term data. The applicant shall provide long-term stability data generated at 30 °C ± 2 °C and 65% RH ± 5% RH, covering at least 12 months at the time of submission, on at least three batches.
Accelerated data. Accelerated data shall be generated at 40 °C ± 2 °C and 75% RH ± 5% RH for 6 months. Accelerated data do not replace long-term data.
Shelf life. The proposed shelf life shall not be longer than the period covered by real-time data unless a written extrapolation is given and justified.
Reporting. A stability report shall give the batch numbers, the pack, the storage conditions, the time points and the results in tables.

law.title: Example Guideline on Leaflets and Labels

clauses.text: Leaflet language. The patient information leaflet shall be provided in Arabic and in English. The two versions shall carry the same information.
clauses.section_path: Part 3 > Patient information leaflet > 3.1 Leaflet language

clauses.text: Leaflet dose statement. The dose, the strength, the units and the frequency of administration shall be stated clearly, and shall be the same in every language version of the leaflet.
clauses.section_path: Part 3 > Patient information leaflet > 3.2 Leaflet dose statement

clauses.text: Leaflet warnings. Warnings shall be given in the same order and with the same force in every language version of the leaflet.
clauses.section_path: Part 3 > Patient information leaflet > 3.3 Leaflet warnings

clauses.text: Outer carton text. The outer carton shall state the storage conditions in Arabic and in English. The maximum storage temperature shall be given in degrees Celsius.
clauses.section_path: Part 4 > Outer packaging > 4.1 Outer carton text
